However more research is needed, looking into the potential downsides. (Lee, 
2021), highlights in his review that half of the articles analysed do not 
investigate the limitations of Microlearning. He highlights two areas where more 
research is needed: (1) usability and UIX optimisation (2) its effectiveness in 
higher order cognitive processing, which may make it ineffective for larger 
topics.  
In summary the research indicates that microlearning provides a fast and 
engaging method of learning, that could improve motivation, knowledge 
retention, and student pass rates. However, the long-term effectiveness for 
large topics is unknown, and its small byte sizzed nature may limit higher order 
cognitive processing my not challenging the student enough. Microlearning 
seems to mostly fit in well with cognitive load theory by limiting extraneous 
load, but without a widely agreed upon framework, germane and intrinsic load 
are very much implementation dependent. 
2.3.4 Spaced Repetition Educational Framework 
Defines spaced practice as the repeated study of a certain topic separated over a 
period of time or after a certain number of other study sessions (Toppino & 
Gerbier, 2014). The paper highlights that memory retention can be improved 
when information is collected over a period of time. It is also noted that 
rehearsal of information (spaced repetition), may improve memory, the 
effectiveness of this is highly dependent on how spaced the rehearsals are. 
The exact spacing between rehearsals is out of the scope of this report, however 
the following paper looks into this area in more detail, using mathematics 
(Tabibian, et al., 2019).
